text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000096 bills 99215 far above what its mostly low-complexity panel predicts, yet the limited charts returned support the billed levels, so the signals conflict.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is consistent with upcoding: the excess 99215 share is concentrated on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and sampled low-complexity 99215s carry routine diagnoses such as UTI, follow-up visits, URI and back pain (e.g., C0065099, C0065101, C0066276). Against that, the returned records support the billed level at a rate better than comparison providers, which would normally point toward legitimate complexity. That support is weakened by C0064844, a 0-condition UTI visit documented as high MDM, and by the note signals: a notable share of notes show problem-list and repeated-time flags, and no audit trail was received to rule out cloned or templated notes. The data-reviewed versus missing lab line mismatch affects only a few notes and is weak evidence. A reviewer should first pull full charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and compare the documented MDM elements to the actual encounter, and should request the EHR audit trail to check for copy-forward or templated time entries."}
